_comment_ConfigurationBoundaries: The sections below establish where configuration binds from. Identity's Authority/Audience are NOT secrets (see EntraIdentityOptions's own doc comment) — they are left empty here deliberately; real values are supplied via environment variables or appsettings.Development.json (untracked) in any real deployment, never committed. Billing/Database/ProviderCredentials remain empty comment-only placeholders — out of scope until their respective future phases. See docs/phase-6.3-backend-foundation.md 'Configuration strategy' and docs/phase-6.4-entra-authentication.md 'Configuration'.

Identity._comment: Microsoft Entra External ID. Authority = tenant's OIDC issuer URL (e.g. https://<tenant>.ciamlogin.com/<tenantId>/v2.0). Audience = this API's application/client ID. Neither is a secret. Left empty here on purpose — see comment above.

Admin._comment: Phase 7.0: the separate admin/workforce authentication boundary (docs/phase-7.0-production-identity-and-account-lifecycle.md §12/§13). Preferred production model is a SEPARATE Microsoft Entra workforce tenant, never the same tenant/audience as the customer Identity:Authority/Identity:Audience above. Neither field is a secret. Left empty here on purpose — no admin API exists yet in this phase.

AccountProvisioning._comment: Phase 7.0: non-secret. Gated just-in-time account-provisioning policy (Option D) — see docs/phase-7.0-production-identity-and-account-lifecycle.md §7. Values below are safe, documented defaults, not product-approved specific thresholds (see that document's §26, still open).

Billing._comment: No real billing provider is activated (Phase 6.6 implements the webhook/subscription-lifecycle boundary only, against NotImplementedBillingProvider). Provider/Environment are non-secret placeholders; WebhookSigningSecret IS a secret and must stay empty here — real values come from environment variables / a secret manager in any real deployment, never a committed value.

Database._comment: PostgreSQL (see docs/phase-6.5-database-decision.md). ConnectionString IS a secret (carries a database password) — it is always empty here and must be supplied only via environment variable / secret manager in any real deployment. Left empty in Development on purpose: the API falls back to in-memory, non-durable repositories when this is unset AND the environment is Development; it refuses to start in any other environment without it (see Program.cs).

ProviderCredentials._comment: Phase 6.8: SubscriptionKey values ARE secrets (the long-lived Azure Cognitive Services master keys) and must always stay empty here — real values come from environment variables / a secret manager in any real deployment, never a committed value. Region is not a secret. An unconfigured provider (empty SubscriptionKey or Region) is simply never registered — /provider-access then fails closed with 'unsupported_provider' for it, never a fabricated credential. Gemini/OpenAI are deliberately absent — see docs/phase-6.8-provider-access-gateway.md for why Gemini has no safe short-lived-credential mechanism to broker.

ProviderAccess._comment: Phase 6.8: non-secret. CredentialLifetimeSeconds is the REQUESTED short-lived-credential lifetime; the actual issued lifetime may be shorter (e.g. Azure's STS tokens are always exactly 10 minutes regardless of what is requested here) — see AzureProviderCredentialIssuer's own doc comment.

TranslationSessions._comment: Phase 6.9: non-secret. LeaseSeconds is the server-side lease window — an Active session with no heartbeat/end within this window since its last observed activity is lazily reconciled to Expired the next time anything touches it. See docs/phase-6.9-usage-metering-and-session-accounting.md.
